s.t: On a hot afternoon, Alice sat with her sister on the river bank.
s.fr: Par un chaud après-midi, Alice s’assit avec sa sœur sur la rive.

s.t: Her sister read a book with no pictures in it.
s.fr: Sa sœur lisait un livre qui n’avait pas d’images.

s.t: A book with no pictures was no good to Alice.
s.fr: Un livre sans images n’était d’aucune utilité pour Alice.

s.t: The sun was hot, and soon Alice was half asleep in the grass.
s.fr: Le soleil était chaud, et bientôt Alice était à moitié endormie dans l’herbe.

paras.summary: On a hot afternoon Alice sits with her sister on the river bank, bored by a book with no pictures, and the hot sun soon has her half asleep in the grass.

s.t: A white rabbit ran past her in the grass.
s.fr: Un lapin blanc passa devant elle dans l’herbe.

s.t: The rabbit took a watch out of its pocket.
s.fr: Le lapin sortit une montre de sa poche.

s.t: It looked at the watch as it ran.
s.fr: Il regarda la montre en courant.

s.t: "I am late!" said the rabbit.
s.fr: « Je suis en retard ! » dit-il.

s.t: Alice got up.
s.fr: Alice se leva.

s.t: She had never seen a rabbit with a watch, or heard one talk.
s.fr: Elle n’avait jamais vu un lapin avec une montre, ni entendu un parler.

paras.summary: A white rabbit runs past, takes a watch from its pocket, says it is late, and Alice gets up amazed, since she has never seen a rabbit with a watch or heard one talk.

s.t: Alice was curious, and she ran after the rabbit across the field.
s.fr: Alice était curieuse, et elle courut après le lapin à travers le champ.

s.t: The rabbit ran on and on and did not stop.
s.fr: Le lapin continua à courir et ne s’arrêta pas.

s.t: It went down a big hole under the hedge.
s.fr: Il descendit dans un grand trou sous la haie.

s.t: Alice went down into the dark hole after it.
s.fr: Alice descendit dans le trou sombre après lui.

s.t: She did not stop to think about the way out.
s.fr: Elle ne s’arrêta pas pour penser à la sortie.

paras.summary: Curious, Alice chases the rabbit across the field and follows it down a big hole under the hedge, without stopping to think about the way out.

s.t: A little way down in the hole, the ground under her was gone.
s.fr: Un peu plus bas dans le trou, le sol sous elle avait disparu.

s.t: Alice fell.
s.fr: Alice tomba.

s.t: She fell down and down in the dark hole.
s.fr: Elle tomba de plus en plus bas dans le trou sombre.

paras.summary: A little way in, the ground vanishes under her, and Alice falls down and down into the dark, and the fall does not stop.

s.t: Alice fell and fell down the dark hole, but the fall did not hurt her.
s.fr: Alice tomba et tomba dans le trou sombre, mais la chute ne lui fit pas mal.

s.t: The hole was deep, but it was not all dark.
s.fr: Le trou était profond, mais il n’était pas entièrement sombre.

s.t: The sides of the hole were full of little cupboards.
s.fr: Les parois du trou étaient pleines de petits placards.

s.t: She fell past the little doors of the cupboards.
s.fr: Elle tomba devant les petites portes des placards.

s.t: As she fell past a cupboard, Alice took a jar from it, but the jar was empty.
s.fr: Comme elle tombait devant un placard, Alice en prit un bocal, mais le bocal était vide.

paras.summary: Alice falls slowly down a deep hole whose sides are full of little cupboards, and as she falls she takes a jar from one of them, but the jar is empty.

s.t: Alice did not drop the empty jar.
s.fr: Alice ne laissa pas tomber le bocal vide.

s.t: She put the jar into the next cupboard as she fell past it.
s.fr: Elle posa le bocal dans le placard suivant en tombant devant lui.

paras.summary: She does not drop the jar, since the white rabbit could be far below her, and instead puts it into the next cupboard as she falls past — the fall leaves time for all of it.

s.t: At last the fall ended, and Alice came down soft on dry leaves, and all was still.
s.fr: Enfin la chute se termina, et Alice atterrit doucement sur des feuilles sèches, et tout était calme.

s.t: She was not hurt at all, and she got up fast.
s.fr: Elle n’était pas blessée du tout, et elle se leva vite.

s.t: The white rabbit was still in front of her, far down a long hall.
s.fr: Le lapin blanc était encore devant elle, loin dans un long couloir.

s.t: "I am so late!" said the rabbit.
s.fr: « Je suis si en retard ! » dit le lapin.

s.t: Alice ran after it, but soon the white rabbit was gone.
s.fr: Alice courut après lui, mais bientôt le lapin blanc avait disparu.

paras.summary: The fall ends softly on dry leaves; Alice gets up unhurt, sees the white rabbit far ahead saying it is so late, and runs after it until it is gone.

s.t: Alice stood alone in the hall, and lamps hung from its roof.
s.fr: Alice se tenait seule dans le couloir, et des lampes pendaient de son plafond.

s.t: There were doors all around the hall.
s.fr: Il y avait des portes tout autour du couloir.

s.t: Alice went to the doors, but the doors did not open.
s.fr: Alice alla aux portes, mais les portes ne s’ouvraient pas.

s.t: Every door in the hall was locked.
s.fr: Chaque porte de la salle était fermée à clé.

paras.summary: Alice stands alone in a long hall with lamps hung from the roof and doors all around, and though she walks from door to door on both sides, every door is locked.

s.t: In the hall stood a little glass table.
s.fr: Dans la salle se trouvait une petite table en verre.

s.t: On the table was a little gold key.
s.fr: Sur la table se trouvait une petite clé en or.

s.t: Alice took the key, but it was far too little for the big doors.
s.fr: Alice prit la clé, mais elle était bien trop petite pour les grandes portes.

s.t: At one end of the hall, Alice saw a curtain.
s.fr: À un bout de la salle, Alice vit un rideau.

s.t: Behind the curtain was a little door.
s.fr: Derrière le rideau se trouvait une petite porte.

paras.summary: Alice finds a little glass table in the hall with a gold key on it; the key is far too little for the big doors, but at one end of the hall she finds a little door behind a curtain.

s.t: Alice turned the gold key in the little door, and the door opened.
s.fr: Alice tourna la clé en or dans la petite porte, et la porte s’ouvrit.

s.t: She went down on her knees and looked through it.
s.fr: Elle se mit à genoux et regarda à travers.

s.t: Through the little door, Alice saw a beautiful garden.
s.fr: À travers la petite porte, Alice vit un beau jardin.

s.t: She saw bright flowers and little rivers of water.
s.fr: Elle vit des fleurs brillantes et de petits ruisseaux d’eau.

s.t: But the little door was too little for Alice.
s.fr: Mais la petite porte était trop petite pour Alice.

s.t: Alice shut the little door, for she could not get through it, and it was locked again.
s.fr: Alice ferma la petite porte, car elle ne pouvait pas passer à travers, et elle était fermée à clé de nouveau.

paras.summary: The gold key turns in the little door, and through it Alice sees a beautiful garden of bright flowers and little rivers, but the door is far too little for her, so she shuts it, and it locks again.

s.t: She stood up and put the key back on the glass table.
s.fr: Elle se leva et remit la clé sur la table en verre.

s.t: A little bottle stood on the table now.
s.fr: Une petite bouteille se trouvait maintenant sur la table.

s.t: The bottle was not there before.
s.fr: La bouteille n’était pas là avant.

s.t: A little paper hung from the bottle, with the words DRINK ME on it.
s.fr: Un petit papier pendait à la bouteille, avec les mots BOIS-MOI dessus.

s.t: Alice was curious, and she drank all that was in the bottle.
s.fr: Alice était curieuse, et elle but tout ce qui était dans la bouteille.

s.t: At once she began to shrink, and she shrank and shrank.
s.fr: Aussitôt elle commença à rétrécir, et elle rétrécit et rétrécit encore.

s.t: Soon Alice was the right size for the little door.
s.fr: Bientôt Alice était de la bonne taille pour la petite porte.

paras.summary: Alice puts the key back on the glass table, where a little bottle now stands that was not there before; its paper says DRINK ME, and when she drinks it all, she shrinks down to the right size for the little door.

s.t: Alice ran back to the little door, but the door was still locked.
s.fr: Alice courut vers la petite porte, mais la porte était encore fermée à clé.

s.t: She had shut it herself, and the key was back on the glass table.
s.fr: Elle l’avait fermée elle-même, et la clé était de nouveau sur la table en verre.

s.t: The little glass table stood high over her head.
s.fr: La petite table en verre se trouvait bien au-dessus de sa tête.

s.t: Alice tried to get up the glass leg of the table.
s.fr: Alice essaya de grimper le pied en verre de la table.

s.t: Her hands slipped on the glass each time.
s.fr: Ses mains glissaient sur le verre à chaque fois.

paras.summary: Alice runs back to the little door, but it is locked, and the key she put back is high on the glass table; she tries to get up the glass leg, but her hands slip each time, and she sees she will never reach it that way.

s.t: Under the table she saw a little glass box with a cake in it.
s.fr: Sous la table elle vit une petite boîte en verre avec un gâteau dedans.

s.t: On the cake were the words EAT ME.
s.fr: Sur le gâteau se trouvaient les mots MANGE MOI.

s.t: Alice ate a little of the cake, but at first she did not grow or shrink.
s.fr: Alice mangea un peu du gâteau, mais au début elle ne grandit pas et ne rétrécit pas.

s.t: She ate all of the cake.
s.fr: Elle mangea tout le gâteau.

paras.summary: Under the table Alice finds a little glass box with a cake in it that says EAT ME, and when a first little taste changes nothing, she eats it all.

s.t: At once Alice began to grow, and she grew fast, up and up.
s.fr: Aussitôt Alice commença à grandir, et elle grandit vite, de plus en plus haut.

s.t: Soon her head came up to the roof of the hall.
s.fr: Bientôt sa tête atteignit le plafond de la salle.

s.t: Alice was a giant now in the hall of doors.
s.fr: Alice était maintenant une géante dans la salle des portes.

s.t: She could take the little key from the glass table now.
s.fr: Elle pouvait maintenant prendre la petite clé sur la table de verre.

paras.summary: Alice grows fast until her head comes up to the roof of the hall; now she is a giant, and she can easily take the little key from the table.

s.t: But she could not put the little key into the little door.
s.fr: Mais elle ne pouvait pas mettre la petite clé dans la petite porte.

s.t: Her hand was far too big for the little door.
s.fr: Sa main était bien trop grande pour la petite porte.

s.t: Alice got down on the floor and looked through the key hole with one eye.
s.fr: Alice s’allongea sur le sol et regarda par le trou de la serrure avec un œil.

paras.summary: But her hand is now far too big to put the key into the little door, and all she can do is look at the garden through the key hole with one eye — big or small, she cannot get in.

s.t: Alice sat down on the floor of the hall and cried and cried.
s.fr: Alice s’assit par terre dans la salle et pleura et pleura.

s.t: Her tears were big tears, for Alice was a giant still.
s.fr: Ses larmes étaient de grosses larmes, car Alice était encore une géante.

s.t: Soon there was a wide pool of tears all around her on the floor.
s.fr: Bientôt il y eut une large mare de larmes tout autour d’elle sur le sol.

s.t: The white rabbit came back into the hall.
s.fr: Le lapin blanc revint dans la salle.

s.t: It had a little fan in one hand.
s.fr: Il avait un petit éventail dans une main.

s.t: The rabbit saw the giant Alice there, and it was afraid.
s.fr: Le lapin vit la géante Alice là, et il eut peur.

s.t: It dropped the little fan and ran from the hall.
s.fr: Il laissa tomber le petit éventail et s’enfuit du couloir.

paras.summary: Still a giant, Alice sits on the floor of the hall and cries, and her giant tears soon make a wide pool; the white rabbit comes back with a little fan, but at the sight of the giant Alice it is afraid, drops the fan, and runs.

s.t: Alice took the fan up and waved it before her hot face.
s.fr: Alice prit l’éventail et l’agita devant son visage chaud.

s.t: As she waved the fan, Alice began to shrink down and down.
s.fr: Tandis qu’elle agitait l’éventail, Alice commença à rétrécir de plus en plus.

s.t: Alice dropped the fan at once, and she shrank no more.
s.fr: Alice laissa tomber l’éventail aussitôt, et elle ne rétrécit plus.

s.t: The key was too big for her little hands now, and it fell by the little door.
s.fr: La clé était trop grande pour ses petites mains maintenant, et elle tomba près de la petite porte.

paras.summary: Alice waves the fan before her hot face and begins to shrink, sees it is the fan that is making her small, and drops it just in time; the key is now too big for her little hands and falls by the little door.

s.t: Alice ran for the little door, but her feet slipped on the wet floor, and she fell into the pool.
s.fr: Alice courut vers la petite porte, mais ses pieds glissèrent sur le sol mouillé, et elle tomba dans le bassin.

s.t: The water of the pool went over her head.
s.fr: L’eau du bassin lui passa par-dessus la tête.

paras.summary: Small again, Alice runs for the little door, but she slips on the wet floor into the pool of her own tears, cried when she was a giant, and the water goes over her head.

s.t: Alice swam and swam, but the pool had grown wide around her.
s.fr: Alice nagea et nagea, mais le bassin s’était élargi autour d’elle.

s.t: When her feet found the ground at last, the hall was gone.
s.fr: Quand ses pieds trouvèrent enfin le sol, le couloir avait disparu.

s.t: Alice walked up out of the water and into the grass.
s.fr: Alice sortit de l’eau et marcha dans l’herbe.

s.t: She stood at the edge of a wood, small and wet from her hair to her feet.
s.fr: Elle se tenait au bord d’un bois, petite et mouillée des pieds à la tête.

paras.summary: She swims and swims across the grown-wide pool until her feet find ground, and when she walks out of the water, the hall is gone and she stands at the edge of a wood, small and wet from her hair to her feet.

s.t: Alice walked into the wood.
s.fr: Alice entra dans le bois.

s.t: She was so small now that the grass of the wood stood high over her head.
s.fr: Elle était si petite maintenant que l’herbe du bois se dressait haut au-dessus de sa tête.

s.t: Soon Alice came to a mushroom that was as high as her head.
s.fr: Bientôt Alice arriva à un champignon qui était aussi haut que sa tête.

s.t: On top of the mushroom sat a big caterpillar.
s.fr: Sur le dessus du champignon était assis un grand chenille.

paras.summary: Alice walks into the wood, so small now that the grass stands high over her head, and comes to a mushroom as high as her head with a big caterpillar sitting on top.

s.t: Alice looked up at it, and the caterpillar looked down at Alice.
s.fr: Alice leva les yeux vers lui, et la chenille baissa les yeux vers Alice.

s.t: It looked at her for a long time and said nothing at all.
s.fr: Elle la regarda pendant longtemps et ne dit rien du tout.

s.t: "Who are you?" the caterpillar asked at last.
s.fr: « Qui êtes-vous ? » demanda la chenille à la fin.

s.t: "I do not know now," said Alice.
s.fr: « Je ne sais pas maintenant, » dit Alice.

s.t: "Today I was big, and today I was small."
s.fr: « Aujourd’hui j’étais grande, et aujourd’hui j’étais petite. »

paras.summary: The caterpillar looks down at Alice a long time without a word, then asks who she is, and she says she does not know now, since today she has been both big and small.

s.t: "What size do you want to be?" the caterpillar asked.
s.fr: « Quelle taille veux-tu être ? » demanda la chenille.

s.t: "I want my own right size," said Alice.
s.fr: « Je veux ma propre taille, » dit Alice.

s.t: As it went down into the grass at last, the caterpillar said, "One side will make you grow."
s.fr: Quand elle descendit enfin dans l’herbe, la chenille dit « Un côté te fera grandir. »

s.t: "The other side will make you shrink."
s.fr: « L’autre côté te fera rapetisser. »

s.t: "One side of what?" Alice asked it.
s.fr: « Un côté de quoi ? » lui demanda Alice.

s.t: "Of the mushroom," said the caterpillar, and it was gone in the grass.
s.fr: « Du champignon, » dit la chenille, et elle disparut dans l’herbe.

paras.summary: The caterpillar asks what size she wants to be, and as it goes down into the grass it says that one side will make her grow and the other will make her shrink — one side of the mushroom — and then it is gone before she can ask more.

s.t: Alice put her arms around the mushroom as far as they would go.
s.fr: Alice passa ses bras autour du champignon aussi loin qu’ils pouvaient aller.

s.t: She took a little piece from each side of it, one piece in each hand.
s.fr: Elle prit un petit morceau de chaque côté, un morceau dans chaque main.

s.t: But the two sides of the mushroom looked the same.
s.fr: Mais les deux côtés du champignon semblaient pareils.

paras.summary: Alice reaches around the mushroom and takes a little piece from each side, one in each hand, but the two sides look the same, and she does not know which piece is which.

s.t: Alice bit a little from the piece in her right hand.
s.fr: Alice mordit un peu dans le morceau dans sa main droite.

s.t: At once she began to grow, and she grew fast, up and up and up.
s.fr: Aussitôt elle commença à grandir, et elle grandit vite, de plus en plus haut.

s.t: Her head went up above the green tops of the trees.
s.fr: Sa tête monta au-dessus des sommets verts des arbres.

paras.summary: Alice bites the piece in her right hand and grows fast, up above the tops of the trees into the blue sky, a giant over the wood again.

s.t: Alice was wet from the pool, but the hot sun soon made her dry.
s.fr: Alice était mouillée à cause de la mare, mais le soleil chaud la sécha vite.

s.t: She looked for the white rabbit, but she did not see it.
s.fr: Elle chercha le lapin blanc, mais elle ne le vit pas.

s.t: Far away, over the trees, Alice saw the roof of a little house.
s.fr: Au loin, au-dessus des arbres, Alice vit le toit d’une petite maison.

s.t: But she did not want to be a giant in the wood.
s.fr: Mais elle ne voulait pas être une géante dans la forêt.

paras.summary: The hot sun up there soon dries her, and though she looks for the white rabbit, all she sees far away is the roof of a little house — and she does not want to be a giant in the wood.

s.t: Alice bit a little from the piece in the other hand.
s.fr: Alice mordit un peu du morceau dans l’autre main.

s.t: She shrank so fast that the grass was soon high over her head again.
s.fr: Elle rétrécit si vite que l’herbe fut bientôt bien au-dessus de sa tête.

s.t: After that, Alice was careful.
s.fr: Après cela, Alice fut prudente.

s.t: She took little bites, first from one piece and after that from the other piece.
s.fr: Elle prit de petites bouchées, d’abord d’un morceau et ensuite de l’autre morceau.

s.t: One little bite made her grow, and the next little bite made her shrink.
s.fr: Une petite bouchée la fit grandir, et la bouchée suivante la fit rétrécir.

paras.summary: She bites the other piece and shrinks too far, down under the grass again, so after that she is careful, taking little bites from one piece and then the other, growing and shrinking a little at a time.

s.t: At last Alice stood at her own right size in the wood again.
s.fr: Alice se retrouva enfin à sa propre taille dans le bois.

s.t: The grow piece went into her right pocket, the shrink piece into her left.
s.fr: Le morceau pour grandir alla dans sa poche droite, le morceau pour rétrécir dans sa gauche.

s.t: Alice was curious about the little house far off in the wood.
s.fr: Alice était curieuse au sujet de la petite maison loin dans le bois.

s.t: She went on through the green trees with a piece in each pocket.
s.fr: Elle continua à travers les arbres verts avec un morceau dans chaque poche.

paras.summary: At last Alice stands at her own right size; she puts the grow piece in her right pocket and the shrink piece in her left, so that she can be big or small when she wants, and walks on through the trees, curious about the little house.

s.t: The road went on under the trees.
s.fr: La route continuait sous les arbres.

s.t: As Alice walked, a smile appeared in the air over the road.
s.fr: Tandis qu’Alice marchait, un sourire apparut dans l’air au-dessus de la route.

s.t: It was a wide smile, and there was no cat around it.
s.fr: C’était un large sourire, et il n’y avait pas de chat autour.

s.t: Around the smile, a cat appeared, a little at a time.
s.fr: Autour du sourire, un chat apparut, peu à peu.

s.t: First came the head of the cat, and after that the rest of it.
s.fr: D’abord vint la tête du chat, et après cela le reste de lui.

s.t: Soon a big cat sat in the tree over the road, and it smiled down at Alice.
s.fr: Bientôt un grand chat s’installa dans l’arbre au-dessus de la route, et il sourit à Alice.

paras.summary: On the road under the trees, a wide smile appears in the air with no cat around it, and then a cat appears around the smile a little at a time, head first, until a big smiling cat sits in the tree.

s.t: "Which is the right way to go?" Alice asked the cat.
s.fr: « Quel est le bon chemin ? » Alice demanda au chat.

s.t: "Where do you want to go?" the cat asked in a soft voice.
s.fr: « Où voulez-vous aller ? » demanda le chat d’une voix douce.

s.t: "I do not know," said Alice.
s.fr: « Je ne sais pas, » dit Alice.

s.t: "If you do not know, any road will do," said the cat.
s.fr: « Si vous ne savez pas, n’importe quel chemin fera l’affaire, » dit le chat.

s.t: "That way lives a hatter," it said.
s.fr: « Par là habite un chapelier, » dit-il.

s.t: "The other way lives a hare."
s.fr: « De l’autre côté habite un lièvre. »

s.t: "They are both strange," the cat said.
s.fr: « Ils sont tous les deux étranges, » dit le chat.

paras.summary: Alice asks which is the right way to go, and the cat asks where she wants to go; when she does not know, it says any road will do, and tells her a hatter lives down one road and a hare down the other, and that both are strange.

s.t: Alice wanted to see the hare, so she took that road.
s.fr: Alice voulait voir le lièvre, alors elle prit ce chemin-là.

s.t: When Alice looked back, the cat faded away, a little at a time.
s.fr: Quand Alice regarda en arrière, le chat disparut peu à peu.

s.t: Its tail went first, and after that the rest of it.
s.fr: Sa queue disparut en premier, et après cela le reste de lui.

s.t: At last only the wide smile hung in the air over the road.
s.fr: À la fin, seul le large sourire resta suspendu dans l’air au-dessus de la route.

s.t: The smile hung there alone for a time, and after that it faded away too.
s.fr: Le sourire resta là seul pendant un moment, et après cela il s’effaça aussi.

paras.summary: Alice takes the road to the hare, and when she looks back, the cat fades away a little at a time, tail first, until only the wide smile hangs alone in the air — and after a time that fades too, leaving Alice to say to herself what a strange thing a smile with no cat is.

chapterList.title: The Tea Party That Never Ended

s.t: Soon Alice came to the little house, and before it, under a tree, stood a long table.
s.fr: Bientôt Alice arriva à la petite maison, et devant elle, sous un arbre, se trouvait une longue table.

s.t: Cups and cups stood all down the long table.
s.fr: Des tasses et des tasses s’alignaient tout le long de la grande table.

s.t: The hatter and the hare sat at one end, and a dormouse sat with them, fast asleep at the table.
s.fr: Le chapelier et le lièvre s’assirent à un bout, et un loir s’assit avec eux, profondément endormi à la table.

s.t: The hatter and the hare rested their arms on the dormouse and talked over its head.
s.fr: Le chapelier et le lièvre posèrent leurs bras sur le loir et parlèrent par-dessus sa tête.

paras.summary: Alice reaches the little house, where a long table stands under a tree with cups all down it; the hatter and the hare sit at one end with a dormouse fast asleep beside them, resting their arms on it as they talk.

s.t: "No room at the table!" called the hare when it saw Alice.
s.fr: « Il n’y a pas de place à la table ! » cria le lièvre quand il vit Alice.

s.t: "There is room for me," said Alice.
s.fr: « Il y a de la place pour moi, » dit Alice.

s.t: She sat down in a big chair at the end of the long table.
s.fr: Elle s’assit dans un grand fauteuil au bout de la longue table.

s.t: "What do a watch and a tea table both have?" the hatter asked her.
s.fr: « Qu’est-ce qu’une montre et une table à thé ont en commun ? » lui demanda le chapelier.

s.t: "I do not know," said Alice at last.
s.fr: « Je ne sais pas, » dit Alice à la fin.

s.t: "I do not know it at all," said the hatter.
s.fr: « Je ne le sais pas du tout, » dit le chapelier.

paras.summary: The hare calls out that there is no room, but Alice says there is room for her and sits down; the hatter asks her what a watch and a tea table both have, and neither Alice nor the hatter himself knows the answer at all.

s.t: The hatter took out a watch and looked at it for a long time.
s.fr: Le chapelier sortit une montre et la regarda pendant longtemps.

s.t: "It is six, and it is always six," said the hatter.
s.fr: « Il est six heures, et il est toujours six heures, » dit le chapelier.

s.t: "Six is tea time, so it is always tea time at this table."
s.fr: « Six heures, c’est l’heure du thé, donc il est toujours l’heure du thé à cette table. »

s.t: "We drink tea all day," said the hare.
s.fr: « Nous buvons du thé toute la journée, » dit le lièvre.

s.t: When a cup was dirty, they all moved one chair down the table.
s.fr: Quand une tasse était sale, ils se déplaçaient tous d’une chaise vers le bas de la table.

paras.summary: The hatter's watch says six, and it is always six — always tea time at this table — so they drink tea all day, moving one chair down the table whenever a cup is dirty.

s.t: Alice got no tea at all at the tea party.
s.fr: Alice n’eut pas de thé du tout à la fête du thé.

s.t: "This is the strangest tea party I have ever seen," said Alice, and she got up.
s.fr: « C’est la fête du thé la plus étrange que j’aie jamais vue, » dit Alice, et elle se leva.

s.t: She walked away from the table and did not look back at it.
s.fr: Elle s’éloigna de la table et ne regarda pas en arrière.

s.t: Behind her, the hatter and the hare only moved down one more chair.
s.fr: Derrière elle, le chapelier et le lièvre ne se déplacèrent que d’une chaise de plus.

paras.summary: The dormouse sleeps on through all of it, and Alice gets no tea at all; she calls it the strangest tea party she has ever seen and walks away, and behind her the hatter and the hare simply move down one more chair.

s.t: Alice walked on from the tea party into the wood.
s.fr: Alice continua depuis la fête du thé jusqu’au bois.

s.t: One big tree had a little door in its side.
s.fr: Un grand arbre avait une petite porte dans son flanc.

s.t: She opened the door in the tree and walked in.
s.fr: Elle ouvrit la porte dans l’arbre et entra.

s.t: In the tree there was no tree at all.
s.fr: Dans l’arbre, il n’y avait pas d’arbre du tout.

s.t: Alice was back in the long hall!
s.fr: Alice était de nouveau dans le long couloir !

paras.summary: Walking on from the tea party, Alice finds a big tree with a little door in its side, and when she opens it and walks in, there is no tree inside at all — she is back in the long hall.

s.t: The lamps still hung from the roof, and the glass table stood where it had stood before.
s.fr: Les lampes pendaient encore au plafond, et la table de verre était là où elle avait été avant.

s.t: The little gold key was still on the floor where it had fallen.
s.fr: La petite clé en or était encore sur le sol là où elle était tombée.

s.t: This time, Alice knew what to do.
s.fr: Cette fois, Alice savait quoi faire.

s.t: She took the little gold key and went down on her knees at the little door.
s.fr: Elle prit la petite clé en or et s’agenouilla devant la petite porte.

paras.summary: The lamps and the glass table are as before, the little gold key still lies on the floor where it fell, and this time Alice knows what to do: she takes the key and kneels at the little door.

s.t: Alice turned the gold key, and the little door opened once more.
s.fr: Alice tourna la clé en or, et la petite porte s’ouvrit encore une fois.

s.t: Alice held the little door open with one hand.
s.fr: Alice maintint la petite porte ouverte avec une main.

s.t: With the other hand, she took the little shrink piece from her left pocket.
s.fr: De l’autre main, elle prit le petit morceau rétrécissant de sa poche gauche.

s.t: She bit it once and shrank, with her hand still on the open door.
s.fr: Elle en mordit une fois et rétrécit, avec sa main toujours sur la porte ouverte.

s.t: When the little door stood as high as her head, Alice walked through it into the garden.
s.fr: Quand la petite porte fut aussi haute que sa tête, Alice marcha à travers elle dans le jardin.

paras.summary: She turns the gold key, holds the little door open with one hand, bites the shrink piece from her left pocket with the other, and when the door stands as high as her head, she walks through it into the garden.

s.t: The bright flowers of the garden stood high over her head once more.
s.fr: Les grandes fleurs du jardin s’élevaient bien au-dessus de sa tête une fois de plus.

s.t: Alice took the grow piece from her right pocket and ate a little bite.
s.fr: Alice prit le morceau de croissance de sa poche droite et en mangea une petite bouchée.

s.t: She grew back to her own right size there in the garden.
s.fr: Elle retrouva sa propre taille normale là dans le jardin.

paras.summary: Among bright flowers that stand high over her head, in a garden full of little rivers, Alice eats a bite of the grow piece from her right pocket, grows back to her own right size, and stands at last in the beautiful garden.

s.t: Not far down the garden, Alice came to a tree full of white roses.
s.fr: Pas loin dans le jardin, Alice arriva à un arbre plein de roses blanches.

s.t: Three gardeners stood at the tree, and they painted the white roses red.
s.fr: Trois jardiniers se tenaient près de l’arbre, et ils peignaient les roses blanches en rouge.

s.t: But many of the roses on the tree were still all white.
s.fr: Mais beaucoup de roses sur l’arbre étaient encore toutes blanches.

s.t: "What is all the red for?" Alice asked the three gardeners at the tree.
s.fr: « Pourquoi tout ce rouge ? » demanda Alice aux trois jardiniers près de l’arbre.

s.t: "We planted white roses by mistake, and the queen wanted red," said one gardener.
s.fr: « Nous avons planté des roses blanches par erreur, et la reine voulait du rouge, » dit un jardinier.

s.t: "If the queen sees white roses in her garden, she will have our heads cut off."
s.fr: « Si la reine voit des roses blanches dans son jardin, elle nous fera couper la tête. »

paras.summary: Not far down the garden Alice finds a tree full of white roses, where three gardeners are painting the white roses red though many are still white; they planted white by mistake when the queen wanted red, and if the queen sees white roses, she will have their heads cut off.

s.t: Alice heard a horn far away across the garden.
s.fr: Alice entendit un cor loin là-bas à travers le jardin.

s.t: The gardeners heard it too and went down flat on their faces.
s.fr: Les jardiniers l’entendirent aussi et se jetèrent à plat sur leurs visages.

s.t: Soldiers marched into the garden of red and white roses, two by two.
s.fr: Des soldats marchèrent dans le jardin de roses rouges et blanches, deux par deux.

s.t: Each soldier was a card with two arms and two legs.
s.fr: Chaque soldat était une carte avec deux bras et deux jambes.

s.t: The cards were flat and white, with red hearts on them.
s.fr: Les cartes étaient plates et blanches, avec des cœurs rouges dessus.

s.t: After the card soldiers came the King and Queen of Hearts.
s.fr: Après les soldats-cartes vinrent le Roi et la Reine de Cœur.

paras.summary: A horn is heard across the garden, the gardeners drop flat on their faces, and soldiers march in two by two — each one a flat white card with arms and legs and red hearts on it — followed by the King and Queen of Hearts.

s.t: The Queen of Hearts stopped at the tree and looked at the white and red roses.
s.fr: La Reine de Cœur s’arrêta à l’arbre et regarda les roses blanches et rouges.

s.t: "The roses are still white!" the queen shouted.
s.fr: « Les roses sont encore blanches ! » cria la reine.

s.t: "Off with their heads!" she shouted at the gardeners.
s.fr: « Qu’on leur coupe la tête ! » cria-t-elle aux jardiniers.

s.t: But the queen had turned away to the next tree of roses.
s.fr: Mais la reine s’était déjà détournée vers l’arbre suivant des roses.

paras.summary: The queen stops at the tree, shouts that the roses are still white, and calls for the gardeners' heads, but a moment later she has turned away to the next tree of roses.

s.t: The gardeners ran to Alice, and the three flat cards went into a big garden pot by the tree.
s.fr: Les jardiniers coururent vers Alice, et les trois cartes plates allèrent dans un grand pot de jardin près de l’arbre.

s.t: The soldiers looked for them but could not find them, and soon the queen went on down the garden.
s.fr: Les soldats les cherchèrent mais ne purent pas les trouver, et bientôt la reine continua plus loin dans le jardin.

s.t: "Can you play croquet?" the queen asked Alice.
s.fr: « Savez-vous jouer au croquet ? » la reine demanda à Alice.

s.t: "I can," said Alice, and she walked after the queen to the croquet ground.
s.fr: « Je le peux, » dit-elle, et elle marcha après la reine jusqu’au terrain de croquet.

paras.summary: The gardeners run to Alice, who hides the flat card men in a big garden pot where the soldiers cannot find them, and the queen, going on down the garden, asks Alice if she can play croquet; Alice says she can and follows her to the croquet ground.

s.t: The croquet ground had many players, and the queen and the king played too.
s.fr: Le terrain de croquet avait beaucoup de joueurs, et la reine et le roi jouèrent aussi.

s.t: Every ball and every hoop in the game could get up and walk.
s.fr: Chaque balle et chaque arceau dans le jeu pouvait se lever et marcher.

s.t: The balls of the game were hedgehogs, and each hedgehog was a ball.
s.fr: Les balles du jeu étaient des hérissons, et chaque hérisson était une balle.

s.t: The players hit the balls of the game with flamingos.
s.fr: Les joueurs frappaient les balles du jeu avec des flamants.

paras.summary: On the croquet ground even the king and queen play, and every ball and hoop in the game can get up and walk — the balls are hedgehogs, and the players hit them with flamingos.

s.t: Alice put the head of her flamingo down to the ground to hit her hedgehog.
s.fr: Alice posa la tête de son flamant vers le bas pour frapper son hérisson.

s.t: But the flamingo turned its long neck up and looked at her.
s.fr: Mais le flamant tourna son long cou vers le haut et la regarda.

s.t: Alice laughed at it, and the flamingo would not go down any more.
s.fr: Alice rit de lui, et le flamant ne voulut pas descendre davantage.

s.t: When its head went down once more, her hedgehog had stood up and walked away.
s.fr: Quand sa tête descendit encore une fois, son hérisson s’était levé et avait marché au loin.

paras.summary: Alice puts the head of her flamingo down to hit her hedgehog, but it turns its long neck up and looks at her, and by the time its head goes down once more, her hedgehog has stood up and walked away.

s.t: The hoops of the game were card soldiers, down on their hands and feet.
s.fr: Les arceaux du jeu étaient des soldats de cartes, à quatre pattes.

s.t: When a ball came to them, the card soldiers stood up and walked away too.
s.fr: Quand une balle arrivait vers eux, les soldats de cartes se levaient et s’en allaient aussi.

s.t: All the players played at once, and they took the hedgehogs from each other.
s.fr: Tous les joueurs jouèrent en même temps, et ils se prirent les hérissons les uns aux autres.

s.t: "Off with his head!" the queen shouted at one player, and at the next player after him.
s.fr: « Qu’on lui coupe la tête ! » cria la reine à un joueur, et au joueur suivant après lui.

paras.summary: The hoops are card soldiers down on their hands and feet, and they too stand up and walk away when a ball comes near, while all the players play at once, take the hedgehogs from each other, and hear the queen shout for one head after the next.

s.t: But no head ever came off in the garden.
s.fr: Mais aucune tête ne tomba jamais dans le jardin.

s.t: The king walked behind the queen and said to each player, "You are safe."
s.fr: Le roi marcha derrière la reine et dit à chaque joueur, « Vous êtes en sécurité. »

s.t: The game was over when every hedgehog had walked away from the ground.
s.fr: Le jeu était terminé quand chaque hérisson s’était éloigné du sol.

s.t: As the players stood still, the white rabbit ran in and held a horn up high.
s.fr: Pendant que les joueurs restaient immobiles, le lapin blanc entra en courant et leva un cor bien haut.

s.t: All the cards went out of the garden after the rabbit.
s.fr: Toutes les cartes sortirent du jardin derrière le lapin.

s.t: Alice went out of the garden after them.
s.fr: Alice sortit du jardin derrière eux.

paras.summary: But no head ever comes off in the garden, and the king walks behind the queen telling each player they are safe; the game is over when every hedgehog has walked away, and then the white rabbit runs in with a horn held high, and all the cards go out of the garden after him, with Alice following.

s.t: The cards all went in two long rows to the court of the King and Queen of Hearts.
s.fr: Les cartes allèrent toutes en deux longues rangées vers la cour du Roi et de la Reine de Cœur.

s.t: The king and the queen sat on the high seats above everyone in the court.
s.fr: Le roi et la reine s’assirent sur les hauts sièges au-dessus de tout le monde dans la cour.

s.t: The king was the judge, and he had a white wig on his head.
s.fr: Le roi était le juge, et il avait une perruque blanche sur la tête.

s.t: Small animals sat in two rows at one side of the court that day.
s.fr: De petits animaux étaient assis en deux rangées d’un côté de la cour ce jour-là.

s.t: They were the jury, and they wrote down all that they saw and heard.
s.fr: Ils étaient le jury, et ils notèrent tout ce qu’ils virent et entendirent.

paras.summary: All the cards go to the court of the King and Queen of Hearts, where the king and queen sit on high seats above everyone; the king is the judge in a white wig, and small animals sit in two rows as the jury, writing down all they see.

s.t: In the court, before everyone, stood a little table full of the queen's tarts.
s.fr: Dans la cour, devant tout le monde, se trouvait une petite table pleine des tartes de la reine.

s.t: The Knave of Hearts stood before the high seats, with a card soldier on each side of him.
s.fr: Le Valet de Cœur se tenait devant les sièges élevés, avec un soldat de carte de chaque côté de lui.

s.t: With a long paper in his hand, the white rabbit called, "Quiet in the court!"
s.fr: Un long papier à la main, le lapin blanc appela « Silence dans la cour ! »

s.t: "The Queen of Hearts made the tarts on a hot day," read the rabbit from the paper.
s.fr: « La Reine de Cœur a fait les tartes par une journée chaude, » lut le lapin sur le papier.

s.t: "The Knave of Hearts stole the tarts and took them all far away from the court."
s.fr: « Le Valet de Cœur a volé les tartes et les a emportées très loin de la cour. »

s.t: "I did not steal them!" said the Knave of Hearts to all the court.
s.fr: « Je ne les ai pas volées ! » dit le Valet de Cœur à toute la cour.

paras.summary: A little table full of tarts stands before everyone, and the Knave of Hearts stands before the high seats with a soldier on each side; the white rabbit calls for quiet and reads the charge — the queen made the tarts, and the knave stole them — but the knave says he did not steal them.

s.t: "The court will now hear the first witness," said the king on his high seat.
s.fr: « La cour va maintenant entendre le premier témoin, » dit le roi sur son siège élevé.

s.t: The first witness of the day was the hatter, with a cup of hot tea in his hand.
s.fr: Le premier témoin du jour était le chapelier, avec une tasse de thé chaud à la main.

s.t: "I was not done with my tea," said the hatter.
s.fr: « Je n’avais pas fini mon thé, » dit le chapelier.

s.t: "It is always tea time for me," he said to the king.
s.fr: « C’est toujours l’heure du thé pour moi, » dit-il au roi.

s.t: "What do you know about the tarts?" the king asked the hatter from his high seat.
s.fr: Que savez-vous des tartes ? demanda le roi au chapelier depuis son siège élevé.

paras.summary: The king calls the first witness, the hatter, who comes in with a cup of tea, says he was not done with his tea since it is always tea time for him, and knows nothing at all about the tarts.

s.t: "Nothing at all," said the hatter, and he looked down at his cup of tea.
s.fr: « Rien du tout, » dit le chapelier, et il baissa les yeux sur sa tasse de thé.

s.t: The hands of the hatter shook, and his tea ran over the edge of his cup.
s.fr: Les mains du chapelier tremblèrent, et son thé déborda du bord de sa tasse.

s.t: "You can go," said the king, and the hatter ran out of the court and far away.
s.fr: « Vous pouvez partir, » dit le roi, et le chapelier courut hors du tribunal et très loin.

s.t: The white rabbit looked at the long paper again, and Alice was next on the paper.
s.fr: Le lapin blanc regarda encore le long papier, et Alice était la suivante sur le papier.

paras.summary: The hatter's hands shake so that tea runs over the edge of his cup, and when the king lets him go, he runs out of the court; then the rabbit looks at the paper, and the next name on it is Alice.

s.t: Alice stood up, and everyone in the court looked at her at once.
s.fr: Alice se leva, et tout le monde dans le tribunal la regarda en même temps.

s.t: "What do you know about the tarts?" the king asked her before all the court.
s.fr: « Que savez-vous des tartes ? » lui demanda le roi devant tout le tribunal.

s.t: "Nothing at all about them," said Alice to the king.
s.fr: « Rien du tout à leur sujet, » dit Alice au roi.

s.t: "That is important," said the king to the jury.
s.fr: « C’est important, » dit le roi au jury.

s.t: "The king means it is not important," said the white rabbit, and he looked at the king.
s.fr: « Le roi veut dire que ce n’est pas important, » dit le lapin blanc, et il regarda le roi.

s.t: The small animals of the jury wrote down both of the words.
s.fr: Les petits animaux du jury écrivirent les deux mots.

paras.summary: Alice stands up before the whole court, and when she tells the king she knows nothing at all about the tarts, he calls that important; the rabbit says the king means it is not important, and the small animals of the jury write down both words.

s.t: The white rabbit stood up again with one more paper in his hand.
s.fr: Le lapin blanc se leva de nouveau avec un autre papier dans sa main.

s.t: "It is a poem about the tarts," said the rabbit to the court.
s.fr: « Il s’agit d’un poème sur les tartes, » dit le lapin à la cour.

s.t: But the Knave of Hearts was not in the poem at all.
s.fr: Mais le Valet de Cœur n’était pas du tout dans le poème.

s.t: "This poem means nothing at all," said Alice to all the court.
s.fr: « Ce poème ne signifie rien du tout, » dit Alice à toute la cour.

s.t: "If it means nothing, we can all go home now," said the king.
s.fr: « S’il ne signifie rien, nous pouvons tous rentrer chez nous maintenant, » dit le roi.

paras.summary: The rabbit brings out one more paper, a poem about the tarts in which the knave does not appear at all, and when Alice says the poem means nothing, the king answers that if it means nothing, they can all go home.

s.t: "The jury will now say the verdict," said the king, and the small animals of the jury stood up.
s.fr: « Le jury va maintenant annoncer le verdict, » dit le roi, et les petits animaux du jury se levèrent.

s.t: "No!" the queen shouted, and the court went quiet all at once.
s.fr: « Non ! » cria la reine, et la cour devint silencieuse tout à coup.

s.t: "Punishment first, and the verdict after," said the queen to all the court.
s.fr: « La punition d’abord, et le verdict après, » dit la reine à toute la cour.

s.t: "That is not right," said Alice, and she stood still.
s.fr: « Ce n’est pas juste, » dit Alice, et elle resta immobile.

s.t: "The punishment cannot come before the verdict," Alice said to the queen and the king.
s.fr: « La punition ne peut pas venir avant le verdict, » dit Alice à la reine et au roi.

paras.summary: The king asks the jury for the verdict, but the queen shouts that the punishment comes first and the verdict after, and Alice stands her ground and says that is not right — the punishment cannot come before the verdict.

s.t: "Off with her head!" the queen shouted at Alice, and the court went quiet again.
s.fr: « Qu’on lui coupe la tête ! » cria la reine à Alice, et la cour devint silencieuse de nouveau.

s.t: Two rows of card soldiers marched at Alice to take hold of her.
s.fr: Deux rangées de soldats de cartes marchèrent vers Alice pour la saisir.

s.t: Alice put her hand into her right pocket, and the last piece of the mushroom was still there.
s.fr: Alice mit sa main dans sa poche droite, et le dernier morceau du champignon était encore là.

s.t: Alice ate it all at once, and she began to grow and grow, up and up.
s.fr: Alice mangea tout cela d’un seul coup, et elle commença à grandir et grandir, de plus en plus.

paras.summary: The queen shouts for Alice's head, and two rows of card soldiers march at her; Alice puts her hand into her right pocket, finds the last piece of the mushroom still there, eats it all, and begins to grow and grow.

s.t: Alice grew and grew, up and up, before the high seats of the little court.
s.fr: Alice grandit et grandit, de plus en plus, devant les hauts sièges de la petite cour.

s.t: Her head went up above the high seats and above the court.
s.fr: Sa tête monta au-dessus des hauts sièges et au-dessus de la cour.

s.t: The king and the queen looked small under her now, and the court looked small too.
s.fr: Le roi et la reine semblaient petits sous elle maintenant, et la cour semblait petite aussi.

s.t: The card soldiers stopped where they stood, every one of them.
s.fr: Les soldats de cartes s’arrêtèrent là où ils se tenaient, chacun d’eux.

paras.summary: Alice grows and grows before the high seats until her head is above them, the king and queen look small under her, the card soldiers stop where they stand, and she is a giant in the little court.

s.t: The small animals of the jury ran from their seats and away out of the court.
s.fr: Les petits animaux du jury coururent de leurs sièges et sortirent de la cour.

s.t: The white rabbit dropped his long paper and ran from the court.
s.fr: Le lapin blanc laissa tomber son long papier et courut hors de la cour.

s.t: "Off with her head!" the queen shouted up one more time at the giant Alice.
s.fr: « Qu’on lui coupe la tête ! » cria la reine une fois de plus vers la géante Alice.

s.t: But not one card soldier moved a step.
s.fr: Mais pas un soldat de cartes ne bougea d’un pas.

s.t: The queen looked up at the giant Alice and went one step back.
s.fr: La reine leva les yeux vers la géante Alice et recula d’un pas.

paras.summary: The jury animals run from their seats and the white rabbit drops his paper and runs; the queen shouts one more time for Alice's head, but no soldier moves a step, and the queen herself steps back.

s.t: "I am not afraid of you now," said Alice from high above them.
s.fr: « Je n’ai pas peur de vous maintenant, » dit Alice de très haut au-dessus d’eux.

s.t: "You are only a deck of cards, all of you!"
s.fr: « Vous êtes seulement un jeu de cartes, vous tous ! »

s.t: At that, the whole deck of cards flew up into the air at once.
s.fr: À cela, tout le jeu de cartes s’envola dans l’air d’un seul coup.

s.t: The king, the queen, the knave, and all the card soldiers were up in the air.
s.fr: Le roi, la reine, le valet, et tous les soldats de cartes étaient en l’air.

paras.summary: From high above them Alice says she is not afraid of them, for they are only a deck of cards — and at that, the whole deck flies up into the air, king, queen, knave, and soldiers all.

s.t: The whole court of cards came down at Alice from the air.
s.fr: Toute la cour de cartes descendit sur Alice depuis l’air.

s.t: Alice cried out and hit at them as they fell all around her in the air.
s.fr: Alice cria et les frappa tandis que elles tombaient tout autour d’elle dans l’air.

s.t: But the cards came down soft and dry on her face, again and again.
s.fr: Mais les cartes tombèrent douces et sèches sur son visage, encore et encore.

s.t: Alice shut her eyes as the soft cards fell all around her.
s.fr: Alice ferma les yeux tandis que les cartes douces tombaient tout autour d’elle.

paras.summary: The whole court of cards comes down at her, and Alice cries out and hits at them as they fall, but the cards land soft and dry on her face, again and again, until she shuts her eyes.

s.t: Alice opened her eyes.
s.fr: Alice ouvrit les yeux.

s.t: Her head was in her sister's lap, on the grass of the river bank.
s.fr: Sa tête était sur les genoux de sa sœur, sur l’herbe de la rive.

s.t: Dry leaves fell from the tree, and they fell soft on her face.
s.fr: Des feuilles sèches tombèrent de l’arbre, et elles tombèrent douces sur son visage.

s.t: Her sister took the dry leaves from Alice's hair.
s.fr: Sa sœur prit les feuilles sèches des cheveux d’Alice.

s.t: "Wake up, Alice," said her sister in a soft voice.
s.fr: « Réveille-toi, Alice, » dit-elle d’une voix douce.

s.t: "You slept the whole afternoon in the grass."
s.fr: « Tu as dormi tout l’après-midi dans l’herbe. »

paras.summary: Alice opens her eyes with her head in her sister's lap on the river bank, where dry leaves are falling soft from the tree onto her face; her sister takes them from her hair and tells her she has slept the whole afternoon.

s.t: The sky was blue over the river, and the evening sun was warm on the grass.
s.fr: Le ciel était bleu au-dessus de la rivière, et le soleil du soir était chaud sur l’herbe.

s.t: A bird flew over the river and away over the field.
s.fr: Un oiseau vola au-dessus de la rivière et au-loin au-dessus du champ.

s.t: There was no white rabbit and no card in the grass now.
s.fr: Il n’y avait pas de lapin blanc et pas de carte dans l’herbe maintenant.

s.t: Alice looked at the blue sky and at the river for a time.
s.fr: Alice regarda le ciel bleu et la rivière un moment.

paras.summary: The sky is blue over the river, the evening sun is warm, a bird flies away over the field, and there is no white rabbit and no card anywhere in the grass; Alice looks at the sky and the river for a time.

s.t: "I had a strange dream!" said Alice to her sister.
s.fr: « J’ai fait un rêve étrange ! » dit Alice à sa sœur.

s.t: She told her sister the whole story of the dream, from the white rabbit to the deck of cards.
s.fr: Elle raconta à sa sœur toute l’histoire du rêve, du lapin blanc au jeu de cartes.

s.t: Her sister laughed at the story of the dream and kissed her.
s.fr: Sa sœur rit de l’histoire du rêve et l’embrassa.

paras.summary: Alice says she had a strange dream and tells her sister the whole story, from the white rabbit to the deck of cards, and about the pool of tears and the cat that faded away, and her sister laughs at the story and kisses her.

s.t: "It is late now, and it is time for tea," said her sister.
s.fr: « Il est tard maintenant, et c’est l’heure du thé, » dit-elle.

s.t: In her dream, Alice got no tea at all, so this time she would drink her tea at home.
s.fr: Dans son rêve, Alice n’avait pas eu de thé du tout, alors cette fois elle boirait son thé chez elle.

s.t: Alice and her sister got up from the grass and walked home over the field in the last light.
s.fr: Alice et sa sœur se levèrent de l’herbe et rentrèrent chez elles à travers le champ dans la dernière lumière.

s.t: Alice ran over the grass after her sister, home to tea.
s.fr: Alice courut sur l’herbe après sa sœur, pour rentrer prendre le thé.

paras.summary: Her sister says it is late and time for tea; since in the dream Alice got no tea at all, this time she means to drink it at home, and they walk home over the field in the last light, past the hedge where no white rabbit runs now, Alice running after her sister, home to tea.
